subject: biology
title: Model Question Paper 1
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 80 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.

MCQs carry 1 mark; objective questions carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each); very short answers carry 2 marks (30–50 words); short answers 3 marks (50–80 words); long answers 5 marks (80–120 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Name the modification: (a) Rhizophora roots coming up from the marsh (b) Roots of Cuscuta.
Fill in the blank: Conjoint, collateral and open vascular bundles are found in ______ stem.
State true or false: (a) Nitrogen fixation is an oxidative process. (b) Leghemoglobin is formed by the symbiosis of Rhizobium and the legume.
Name the two phases of photosynthesis and where each occurs.
questions.answer: Light reaction in the thylakoids (grana) and dark reaction in the stroma.

questions.q: Name the process in which (a) Pyruvic acid is converted into acetyl CoA (b) NADH is oxidised in the mitochondrial membrane.
questions.answer: (a) Link (oxidative decarboxylation) reaction. (b) Oxidative phosphorylation (respiratory chain).

questions.q: Name the two types of lymphocytes and their site of development.
questions.answer: B-cells and T-cells, both developing in the bone marrow.

questions.q: Name the three layers of the eyeball and the three meninges.
questions.answer: Sclera, choroid and retina; dura mater, arachnoid and pia mater.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks (any two): (a) ______ and ______ are devices that ensure self-pollination. (b) ______ and ______ are adaptations to promote cross-pollination.
questions.answer: (a) Cleistogamy and homogamy. (b) Dichogamy and self-sterility (also unisexuality).

questions.q: A is an association between maternal and foetal tissue. B is a tough structure which serves as the blood vascular connection between the foetus and the uterine wall. The embryo is enclosed in a sac C filled with D. Fill in the blanks (any two).
questions.answer: A: placenta. B: umbilical cord. C: amnion. D: amniotic fluid (shock absorber).

questions.q: State true or false: (a) A male honey bee has a father. (b) Females of birds are heterogametic.
Name the radioactive isotopes used by Hershey and Chase to label (a) protein (b) DNA.
State true or false: (a) A snake can be a secondary as well as a tertiary consumer. (b) Energy flow in an ecosystem is cyclic.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Distinguish between biological and abiological nitrogen fixation.
questions.answer: Biological fixation occurs in living cells through nitrogenase; abiological fixation occurs without living cells, industrially (Haber's process) or naturally (lightning).

questions.q: What is Kranz anatomy? In which plants is it found?
questions.answer: A wreath-like arrangement of large bundle sheath cells around the vascular bundles with dimorphic chloroplasts, found in C4 plants such as maize and sugarcane.

questions.q: Why do muscles pain during prolonged exercise?
questions.answer: Due to anaerobic respiration, lactic acid accumulates in the muscles.

questions.q: Write the steps of blood clotting in short.
questions.answer: Platelets release thromboplastin; with Ca++ it converts prothrombin to thrombin; thrombin changes fibrinogen to fibrin, which entangles RBCs and forms a clot.

questions.q: What is the function of the yellow spot and the blind spot?
questions.answer: The yellow spot is the place of sharpest vision; the blind spot has no sensory cells and an image falling on it is not seen.

questions.q: Differentiate between epigeal and hypogeal germination (one example each).
questions.answer: In epigeal the cotyledons come above the ground (castor); in hypogeal they stay underground (maize).

questions.q: Write the hormonal roles of FSH and LH in the female menstrual cycle.
questions.answer: FSH stimulates follicle growth and oestrogen secretion; LH causes ovulation and formation of the corpus luteum.

questions.q: What is a human karyotype?
questions.answer: The arrangement of the 23 pairs of human chromosomes in seven groups A to G by size and centromere position.

questions.q: Write the anticodon of codon (i) AGU and (ii) UGC.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Write any three characteristics of fungi.
questions.answer: They are heterotrophic eukaryotes with chitinous cell walls; the body is made of hyphae forming a mycelium; they feed by absorption and reproduce by spores and conjugation.

questions.q: Explain the structure of a neuron.
questions.answer: A cell body with nucleus and Nissl granules, short branched dendrites receiving impulses, a long axon with end branches carrying impulses away and a myelin sheath with nodes of Ranvier.

questions.q: State and explain Mendel's law of independent assortment with a cross.
questions.answer: The genes of different characters assort independently. TTRR × ttrr gives TtRr in F1; F2 gives 9 tall red : 3 tall white : 3 dwarf red : 1 dwarf white.

questions.q: Describe the deficiency diseases caused by vitamins B1, C and D.
questions.answer: B1: beri-beri (pain in the limbs, paralysis); C: scurvy (bleeding gums, joint pain); D: rickets in children (bow legs) and osteomalacia in adults.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Write the differences between DNA and RNA. Write the names of the different types of RNA along with their functions.
questions.answer: Differences: sugar, base, strands and function. mRNA carries the message from DNA to ribosomes; tRNA brings amino acids and has an anticodon; rRNA forms the ribosome and takes part in protein synthesis.

questions.q: Describe antigens and antibodies and the types of immune response.
questions.answer: Antigen properties and epitopes; antibody structure and classes; non-specific and specific (cell-mediated and humoral) responses.
